::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Is it acceptable to hyphenate people’s names?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/15811/is-it-acceptable-to-hyphenate-people-s-names), asked by anon on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-04-14; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> In some circumstances, for example, `B.~Alexander` may result in _B.&nbsp;Alexan-_`newline`_der_.  Is this acceptable?
>
> If not, is there an elegant way to suppress it?  (`\hyphenation` is too cumbersome and sometimes inflexible.)
:::

Whether proper names may or should not be hyphenated is a matter of style.  I found several publishing houses that discourage it, among them [University of Houston](http://www.uh.edu/policies/editorialstyle/h/index.php).  UH says their style comes from the [Associated Press Stylebook][1] (non-free).

My university follows the *Chicago Manual of Style*, and they recommend (paragraph 7.42 if you have access):

1. Break lines between elements of the name where possible. For instance, between given name and family name, or if the family name is hyphenated, at the hyphen. It has examples of multiple initials followed by a last name, and recommends breaking between the initials and last name: `R.J./Drofnats` or `B./Alexander`. Just not between consecutive initials.

2. If that is not possible, consult a dictionary for the acceptable hyphenation point. CMOS refers to Webster's dictionary. The entry for [Alexander][2] gives `Al·​ex·​an·​der`.

3. If that is not possible, consult a pronunciation guide for the name and break the line between syllables. 

4. As a last resort, break before a vowel.

  [1]: http://www.apstylebook.com/
  [2]: https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/alexander
